  1. Power on the unit and let it get to a point where it is moving the head and yank the cord. You want to unlock the head.
  2. Take a paper towel and fold it to the size of the head nozzle area on the bottom.
  3. Soak it in window cleaner.
  4. Flatten it well and lay it in the area the head swipes past.
  5. Move the head so it's over the paper towel. You're going to have to play with this to get the right size AND thickness of the paper towel.
  6. Let it soak for a little bit.
  7. Run the head back and forth gently. Don't let the towel bind up under it.
  8. Let it set again.
  9. Move the head to the middle of the paper towel.
  10. Gently pick up both ends of the towel and swipe it back and forth under the head, gently pulling up. Like you're shining your shoes with a towel but slowly.
  11. Let it set.
  12. Take a q-tip, dab it in rubbing alcohol. Gently swab the nozzle holes and be sure to get just a little in there.
  13. Take a can of compressed air and gently spray those holes.
  14. Repeat the q-tip dabbing and air spraying at least 3 times.
  15. Put in some ink (not off brand, the real deal)
  16. Let the cartridges prime and print a nozzle check.
  17. Run cleaning function
  18. Print a nozzle test.
  19. Repeat nozzle check and cleaning until it either works or you run out of ink.

If you run out of ink, you're printer is hosed, treat it properly next time.
